grade.first_issue: No decisive defect or grading cap applies. The parenthetical suggesting that h equals lcm(m,n) “always” is literally inaccurate, but the preceding case analysis already proves that at least one replacement entry exceeds 1, so the deletion-test carve-out makes this non-load-bearing.
grade.summary: The lexicographically decreasing potential (total number of prime factors, number of entries greater than 1) correctly proves termination and, together with positivity of the total prime-factor count, proves that exactly one nonunit remains. Primewise valuations undergo the subtractive Euclidean transformation, preserving their global gcd; at a terminal board this invariant is exactly each valuation of M, so M is uniquely determined by the initial board.
strengths: The potential function is well-founded and strictly decreases under every move.
Both gcd cases are correctly handled to establish termination and persistence of a nonunit.
The primewise valuation transformation is computed correctly.
The invariant reconstructs the terminal integer and proves independence from all choices.

errors.description: The phrase “h = lcm(m,n) > 1 always” is false literally, since h=lcm(m,n)/gcd(m,n) and may equal 1. This does not affect the proof because the preceding two cases independently show that either g>1 or, when g=1, h=mn>1.
